records.source: וַיָּ֣מָת שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וַיִּקָּבְצ֤וּ כָל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיִּסְפְּדוּ־ל֔וֹ וַיִּקְבְּרֻ֥הוּ בְּבֵית֖וֹ בָּרָמָ֑ה וַיָּ֣קָם דָּוִ֔ד וַיֵּ֖רֶד אֶל־מִדְבַּ֥ר פָּארָֽן׃ס
records.gloss: And died Samuel, and gathered all Israel and mourned for him and buried him in his house in Ramah. And arose David and went down to [the] wilderness of Paran.
pieces: Samuel died, and all Israel gathered and mourned for him. They buried him at his home in Ramah. Then David got up and went down to the wilderness of Paran.

L.1: And Samuel died, and all Israel gathered together and mourned for him, and they buried him at his house in Ramah. And David arose and went down to the wilderness of Paran.

R.1: Samuel died. All the people of Israel came together and mourned for him, and they buried him at his home in the town of Ramah. Then David left and went down to the wilderness of Paran.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Paran, as the Hebrew text reads
alternatives: the wilderness of Maon (the Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has Paran, the wide wilderness far to the south, between Sinai and Kadesh (Numbers 10:12; 13:26). Most manuscripts of the ancient Greek translation read "Maon", the wilderness where David had been hiding (23:24-25) and where this story takes place (verse 2). Maon fits the story more easily; Paran would mean that after Samuel's death David moved much farther away from Saul before coming back to the region of Maon. The Hebrew reading is followed.

decisions.choice: buried him at his house: on his family property in Ramah
decisions.reason: Ramah was Samuel's home town, where he lived and judged (7:17). "At his house" probably means in the family burial place on his own land, not inside the building. His death is mentioned again in 28:3.

decisions.choice: all Israel mourned for him: the nation honors its prophet and judge
decisions.reason: The whole people mourn Samuel as they mourned Moses and Aaron (Deuteronomy 34:8; Numbers 20:29). He had led Israel since his youth (3:20; 7:15).

decisions.choice: the town of Ramah
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the town of" so that the name is clear.

records.heading: The death of Samuel

records.source: וְאִ֨ישׁ בְּמָע֜וֹן וּמַעֲשֵׂ֣הוּ בַכַּרְמֶ֗ל וְהָאִישׁ֙ גָּד֣וֹל מְאֹ֔ד וְל֛וֹ צֹ֥אן שְׁלֹֽשֶׁת־אֲלָפִ֖ים וְאֶ֣לֶף עִזִּ֑ים וַיְהִ֛י בִּגְזֹ֥ז אֶת־צֹאנ֖וֹ בַּכַּרְמֶֽל׃
records.gloss: And a man [was] in Maon, and his business [was] in Carmel, and the man [was] great very, and to him [were] sheep three thousand and a thousand goats; and it was in shearing his sheep in Carmel.
pieces: There was a man in Maon whose property was at Carmel. He was very rich: he owned 3,000 sheep and 1,000 goats. And he was shearing his sheep at Carmel.

L.2: And [there was] a man in Maon whose business [was] in Carmel, and the man [was] very great; and he had 3,000 sheep and 1,000 goats. And he was shearing his sheep in Carmel.

R.2: There was a man from the town of Maon who had land near the town of Carmel. He was very rich. He owned 3,000 sheep and 1,000 goats. At that time he was at Carmel, having his sheep sheared.

decisions.choice: Maon and Carmel: two towns in the hill country of Judah
decisions.reason: Maon and Carmel lay a few miles apart, south of Hebron (Joshua 15:55). This Carmel is not Mount Carmel on the northern coast (1 Kings 18:19). Saul had set up a monument for himself at this Carmel (15:12).

decisions.choice: his business: his work and property
decisions.reason: The word means "work" or "what one does", and here the land and flocks that were his livelihood. He lived in Maon but kept his herds and pasture at Carmel.

decisions.choice: great: wealthy
decisions.reason: "Great" here means rich and important, as of Isaac in Genesis 26:13 and Barzillai in 2 Samuel 19:33. The size of his flocks shows it.

decisions.choice: shearing: a time of feasting
decisions.reason: Sheep were sheared in spring, and shearing was a festival with food and drink, when owners were expected to be generous (verses 8, 36; Genesis 38:12; 2 Samuel 13:23-28).

decisions.choice: property at Carmel, very rich (Balanced); had land near, very rich (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the plain sense of "business" and "great" (m2, m3).

records.heading: Nabal refuses David, and Abigail intervenes

records.source: וְשֵׁ֤ם הָאִישׁ֙ נָבָ֔ל וְשֵׁ֥ם אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ אֲבִגָ֑יִל וְהָאִשָּׁ֤ה טֽוֹבַת־שֶׂ֨כֶל֙ וִ֣יפַת תֹּ֔אַר וְהָאִ֥ישׁ קָשֶׁ֛ה וְרַ֥ע מַעֲלָלִ֖ים וְה֥וּא כָלִבִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And [the] name of the man [was] Nabal, and [the] name of his wife [was] Abigail; and the woman [was] good of insight and beautiful of form, and the man [was] hard and evil of deeds; and he [was] a Calebite.
pieces: The man's name was Nabal, and his wife's name was Abigail. She was a woman of good sense and beautiful in appearance, but her husband was harsh and his dealings were evil. He was a descendant of Caleb.

L.3: And the name of the man [was] Nabal, and the name of his wife [was] Abigail. And the woman [was] good of understanding and beautiful of form, but the man [was] harsh and evil in deeds; and he [was] a Calebite.

R.3: The man's name was Nabal, and his wife's name was Abigail. She was wise and beautiful. But Nabal was hard to deal with, and he did evil things. He belonged to the family of Caleb.

decisions.choice: Nabal: a name that sounds like the word for "fool"
decisions.reason: As an ordinary word, *naval* means a fool, not someone slow of mind but someone who acts without regard for God or for other people (Psalm 14:1; Isaiah 32:5-6). The name may once have had another meaning, but the story hears it as "fool", and Abigail says so in verse 25.

decisions.choice: good of understanding: sensible and wise
decisions.reason: The word means insight or prudence, the practical good sense that knows what to do. Abigail shows it in verses 18-31, and David praises her judgment (verse 33).

decisions.choice: harsh and evil in deeds: hard to deal with and bad in his dealings
decisions.reason: "Hard" describes a man who is stubborn and rough with others. "Evil in deeds" speaks of how he treats people, which the story goes on to show (verses 10-11, 17).

decisions.choice: a Calebite: the reading the scribes marked
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) can be read "like his heart", that is, a man who does as he pleases; the reading the scribes marked to be read aloud (qere) is "a Calebite", a member of the clan of Caleb, who had received Hebron and the land around it (Joshua 14:13-14; 15:13). The clan name also sounds like the word for "dog", which may be a further hint about Nabal's character.

decisions.choice: a descendant of Caleb; belonged to the family of Caleb
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "Calebite" means.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע דָּוִ֖ד בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר כִּֽי־גֹזֵ֥ז נָבָ֖ל אֶת־צֹאנֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And heard David in the wilderness that [was] shearing Nabal his sheep.
pieces: In the wilderness David heard that Nabal was shearing his sheep.

L.4: And David heard in the wilderness that Nabal [was] shearing his sheep.

R.4: David was in the wilderness, and he heard that Nabal was shearing his sheep.

decisions.choice: shearing: a time of plenty and generosity
decisions.reason: At shearing time an owner had food on hand and was expected to share it (verse 2). David sees a fair moment to ask for a return for his protection (verses 7-8).

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח דָּוִ֖ד עֲשָׂרָ֣ה נְעָרִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד לַנְּעָרִ֗ים עֲל֤וּ כַרְמֶ֨לָה֙ וּבָאתֶ֣ם אֶל־נָבָ֔ל וּשְׁאֶלְתֶּם־ל֥וֹ בִשְׁמִ֖י לְשָׁלֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And sent David ten young men, and said David to the young men, Go up to Carmel, and go to Nabal and ask him in my name for peace.
pieces: So David sent ten young men, and he said to them, "Go up to Carmel, go to Nabal and greet him in my name.

L.5: And David sent ten young men, and David said to the young men, "Go up to Carmel and go to Nabal, and ask him in my name about [his] peace.

R.5: So David sent ten young men. He told them, "Go up to Nabal at Carmel and greet him for me.

decisions.choice: young men: David's fighting men, here sent as messengers
decisions.reason: The word can mean a young man, a servant or a soldier. These are men of David's band (verse 13), and verse 14 calls them messengers.

decisions.choice: ask him about his peace: greet him
decisions.reason: To "ask about someone's peace" is to greet him and ask how he is (10:4; 17:22; 30:21). The greeting is in David's name, so it comes from David himself.

decisions.choice: go up: Carmel lay higher than the wilderness
decisions.reason: The wilderness lay east and below the hill towns, so going to Carmel meant climbing.

decisions.choice: greet him in my name; greet him for me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the greeting idiom (m2).

records.source: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֥ם כֹּ֖ה לֶחָ֑י וְאַתָּ֤ה שָׁלוֹם֙ וּבֵיתְךָ֣ שָׁל֔וֹם וְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־לְךָ֖ שָׁלֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And you will say thus: To life! And you peace, and your house peace, and all that [is] to you peace.
pieces: Say this to him: 'Long life to you! Peace to you, peace to your household, and peace to all that you have.

L.6: And you shall say thus: 'To life! Peace [be] to you, and peace [be] to your house, and peace [be] to all that [is] yours.

R.6: Tell him, 'May you live long! May all be well with you, with your family, and with everything you own.

decisions.choice: To life!: a wish for long life
alternatives: to my brother (with a small change to the letters)
to the one who lives in plenty
decisions.reason: The short phrase is found only here, and its sense is not certain. It is most likely a greeting wishing long life or good fortune. Some ancient translations read it differently, and a small change in the Hebrew letters would give "to my brother", a friendly address.

decisions.choice: peace: well-being of every kind
decisions.reason: *Shalom* is health, safety and prosperity, not only the absence of war. The threefold wish covers Nabal himself, his household and all his property.

decisions.choice: your house: your household
decisions.reason: "House" means the whole household: family, servants and all who depend on him.

decisions.choice: May all be well with you
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "peace" (m2) and joins the three wishes.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֣ה שָׁמַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֥י גֹזְזִ֖ים לָ֑ךְ עַתָּ֗ה הָרֹעִ֤ים אֲשֶׁר־לְךָ֙ הָי֣וּ עִמָּ֔נוּ לֹ֣א הֶכְלַמְנ֗וּם וְלֹֽא־נִפְקַ֤ד לָהֶם֙ מְא֔וּמָה כָּל־יְמֵ֖י הֱיוֹתָ֥ם בַּכַּרְמֶֽל׃
records.gloss: And now I have heard that shearers [are] to you. Now the shepherds who [are] to you were with us; not did we humiliate them, and not was missing to them anything all [the] days of their being in Carmel.
pieces: I have heard that you are shearing. Your shepherds have been with us, and we did not mistreat them. Nothing of theirs went missing the whole time they were at Carmel.

L.7: And now I have heard that you have shearers. Now your shepherds have been with us; we did not humiliate them, and nothing of theirs was missing all the days they were in Carmel.

R.7: I hear that your sheep are being sheared. Your shepherds were with us, and we did not harm them. Nothing was stolen from them the whole time they were at Carmel.

decisions.choice: we did not humiliate them: we did them no harm
decisions.reason: The verb means to shame, insult or hurt someone. Nabal's own servant uses the same word to confirm it (verse 15).

decisions.choice: nothing of theirs was missing: the flocks were protected
decisions.reason: An armed band living in the wilderness could easily have taken animals. Instead David's men guarded the shepherds and flocks (verses 15-16, 21). David now asks for a share of the shearing feast in return.

decisions.choice: in Carmel: in the district around the town
decisions.reason: The shepherds grazed the flocks in the open country around Carmel, where David's men were (verses 15-16).

decisions.choice: mistreat (Balanced); harm (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Humiliate" (Literal) here means to harm or abuse (m1).

records.source: שְׁאַ֨ל אֶת־נְעָרֶ֜יךָ וְיַגִּ֣ידוּ לָ֗ךְ וְיִמְצְא֨וּ הַנְּעָרִ֥ים חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ כִּֽי־עַל־י֥וֹם ט֖וֹב בָּ֑נוּ תְּנָה־נָּ֗א אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּמְצָ֤א יָֽדְךָ֙ לַעֲבָדֶ֔יךָ וּלְבִנְךָ֖ לְדָוִֽד׃
records.gloss: Ask your young men, and they will tell you; and let find the young men favor in your eyes, for on a good day we have come. Give please what will find your hand to your servants and to your son, to David.
pieces: Ask your own young men and they will tell you. So let these young men find favor with you, for we have come on a feast day. Please give whatever you have on hand to your servants and to your son David.'"

L.8: Ask your young men, and they will tell you. So let the young men find favor in your eyes, for we have come on a good day. Please give whatever your hand finds to your servants and to your son, to David.'"

R.8: Ask your own workers, and they will tell you. So please be kind to these young men. We have come at a time of celebration. Please give whatever you can to us, your servants, and to your son David.'"

decisions.choice: a good day: a feast day
decisions.reason: A "good day" is a day of celebration (Esther 8:17; 9:19). Here it is the shearing festival, when hosts were generous (verse 2).

decisions.choice: whatever your hand finds: whatever you have available
decisions.reason: The phrase means whatever is at hand, what one can spare (10:7). David asks for no fixed amount.

decisions.choice: your servants and your son David: respectful, humble address
decisions.reason: David speaks as a dependent to an older and wealthier man: his men are Nabal's "servants" and he himself is Nabal's "son". It is a polite request, not a demand.

decisions.choice: your servants (every level)
decisions.reason: The word names a bondservant, but here David's men use it of themselves out of courtesy, so every level has "your servants", the polite form set for these books.

decisions.choice: your own workers; a time of celebration
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for Nabal's young men and for the feast day (m1).

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ נַעֲרֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד וַיְדַבְּר֧וּ אֶל־נָבָ֛ל כְּכָל־הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה בְּשֵׁ֣ם דָּוִ֑ד וַיָּנֽוּחוּ׃
records.gloss: And came [the] young men of David and spoke to Nabal according to all these words in [the] name of David, and they rested.
pieces: When David's young men arrived, they gave Nabal this whole message in David's name. Then they waited.

L.9: And David's young men came and spoke to Nabal according to all these words in the name of David, and they waited.

R.9: David's young men came and told Nabal everything David had said. Then they waited for his answer.

decisions.choice: they rested: they waited quietly for an answer
decisions.reason: The verb means to rest or settle. The messengers have said all they were told and now wait for Nabal's reply. The ancient Greek translation reads instead that Nabal sprang up, an angry reaction.

decisions.choice: waited for his answer
decisions.reason: Readable says what they waited for.

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַן נָבָ֜ל אֶת־עַבְדֵ֤י דָוִד֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר מִ֥י דָוִ֖ד וּמִ֣י בֶן־יִשָׁ֑י הַיּוֹם֙ רַבּ֣וּ עֲבָדִ֔ים הַמִּתְפָּ֣רְצִ֔ים אִ֖ישׁ מִפְּנֵ֥י אֲדֹנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And answered Nabal the servants of David and said, Who [is] David, and who [is] the son of Jesse? Today many [are] slaves who break away each from before his master(s).
pieces: But Nabal answered David's servants, "Who is David? Who is this son of Jesse? There are many slaves these days who run away from their masters.

L.10: And Nabal answered David's servants and said, "Who [is] David, and who [is] the son of Jesse? Today there are many slaves who break away, each from his master.

R.10: But Nabal answered David's servants, "Who is this David? Who is this son of Jesse? These days lots of slaves are running away from their masters.

decisions.choice: Who is David? Who is the son of Jesse?: contempt, not a real question
decisions.reason: Nabal knows who David is; the questions say he is nobody. The same words are used to reject David's house in 2 Samuel 20:1 and 1 Kings 12:16. Saul too calls David "the son of Jesse" to belittle him (20:27, 31; 22:7-8).

decisions.choice: slaves who break away from their masters: a jab at David
decisions.reason: David had fled from his master Saul (19:10-18). Nabal treats him as a runaway slave and his men as more of the same.

decisions.choice: David's servants: his followers
decisions.reason: The word for servant also names the followers or officers of a leader. Here it is the young men of verse 9.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: Nabal's insult rests on slaves running from their masters, so "slaves" is kept at every level, as the style guide asks where slavery itself is the point.

decisions.choice: David's servants
decisions.reason: As envoys and followers of David they are "servants" at every level.

records.source: וְלָקַחְתִּ֤י אֶת־לַחְמִי֙ וְאֶת־מֵימַ֔י וְאֵת֙ טִבְחָתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר טָבַ֖חְתִּי לְגֹֽזְזָ֑י וְנָֽתַתִּי֙ לַֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי אֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה הֵֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: And will I take my bread and my water and my slaughtered meat which I slaughtered for my shearers and give to men whom not I know where from they [are]?
pieces: Am I to take my bread and my water, and the meat I slaughtered for my shearers, and hand it over to men from who knows where?"

L.11: And shall I take my bread and my water and my meat that I have slaughtered for my shearers, and give [it] to men who I do not know where they [are] from?"

R.11: Should I give away my bread and water, and the meat I have prepared for my workers, to men I know nothing about?"

decisions.choice: shall I take?: a question that expects "no"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no question word, but the sense is a scornful question: of course he will give nothing.

decisions.choice: my bread, my water, my meat, my shearers: Nabal stresses what is his
decisions.reason: Nabal says "my" again and again. He sees only his own property, though David's men had protected it (verse 7).

decisions.choice: my water, as the Hebrew text reads
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation has "my wine" instead of "my water". Wine fits a feast (verses 18, 36), but water was also precious in that dry country. The Hebrew reading is followed.

decisions.choice: the meat I have prepared for my workers
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for the slaughtered meat and the shearers.

records.source: וַיַּהַפְכ֥וּ נַעֲרֵֽי־דָוִ֖ד לְדַרְכָּ֑ם וַיָּשֻׁ֨בוּ֙ וַיָּבֹ֔אוּ וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ ל֔וֹ כְּכֹ֖ל הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: And turned [the] young men of David to their way and returned and came and told him according to all these words.
pieces: So David's young men turned around and went back. When they arrived, they reported all these words to him.

L.12: And David's young men turned on their way and went back, and they came and told him according to all these words.

R.12: So David's young men turned around and went back. They told David everything Nabal had said.

decisions.choice: turned on their way: went back the way they had come
decisions.reason: They left at once, without the gift they had asked for.

decisions.choice: told David everything Nabal had said
decisions.reason: Readable names David and Nabal for clarity.

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ דָּוִ֨ד לַאֲנָשָׁ֜יו חִגְר֣וּ׀אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־חַרְבּ֗וֹ וַֽיַּחְגְּרוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־חַרְבּ֔וֹ וַיַּחְגֹּ֥ר גַּם־דָּוִ֖ד אֶת־חַרְבּ֑וֹ וַֽיַּעֲל֣וּ׀אַחֲרֵ֣י דָוִ֗ד כְּאַרְבַּ֤ע מֵאוֹת֙ אִ֔ישׁ וּמָאתַ֖יִם יָשְׁב֥וּ עַל־הַכֵּלִֽים׃
records.gloss: And said David to his men, Gird on each his sword. And girded on each his sword, and girded on also David his sword; and went up after David about four hundred man, and two hundred remained by the baggage.
pieces: David said to his men, "Every man strap on his sword!" So each of them strapped on his sword, and David strapped on his own as well. About 400 men went up with David, while 200 stayed behind with the supplies.

L.13: And David said to his men, "Each [man] gird on his sword." And each [man] girded on his sword, and David also girded on his sword; and about 400 men went up after David, and 200 stayed with the baggage.

R.13: David told his men, "Everyone, put on your swords!" So they all put on their swords, and David put on his too. About 400 men went with David, and 200 stayed behind to guard the supplies.

decisions.choice: gird on his sword, three times: quick, grim obedience
decisions.reason: The phrase is repeated for the order, for the men and for David himself. The repetition shows how fast and how angrily the band gets ready to fight, in answer to Nabal's insult (verses 10-12).

decisions.choice: the baggage: the band's equipment and supplies
decisions.reason: The word covers equipment, weapons and goods of every kind. A band on the move left part of its men to guard them, as David did again in 30:9-10 and 30:24.

decisions.choice: stayed behind to guard the supplies
decisions.reason: Readable adds why the 200 stayed, which 30:24 makes plain.

records.source: וְלַאֲבִיגַ֨יִל֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת נָבָ֔ל הִגִּ֧יד נַֽעַר־אֶחָ֛ד מֵהַנְּעָרִ֖ים לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֣ה שָׁלַח֩ דָּוִ֨ד מַלְאָכִ֧ים׀מֵֽהַמִּדְבָּ֛ר לְבָרֵ֥ךְ אֶת־אֲדֹנֵ֖ינוּ וַיָּ֥עַט בָּהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And to Abigail [the] wife of Nabal told young man one of the young men, saying, Look, sent David messengers from the wilderness to bless our master, and he screamed at them.
pieces: Meanwhile one of the young men told Abigail, Nabal's wife, "David sent messengers out of the wilderness to greet our master, but he flew at them with insults.

L.14: And one young man of the young men told Abigail, Nabal's wife, saying, "Look, David sent messengers from the wilderness to bless our master, and he screamed at them.

R.14: One of Nabal's servants told Abigail, Nabal's wife, "David sent messengers from the wilderness to greet our master, but Nabal yelled insults at them.

decisions.choice: to bless our master: to greet him
decisions.reason: "Bless" is often used of greeting someone with good wishes (13:10). David's men had come with the greeting of verse 6.

decisions.choice: screamed at them: rushed at them with angry words
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a bird of prey swooping down (14:32; 15:19). Nabal fell on the messengers with abuse.

decisions.choice: one of the young men: one of Nabal's own servants
decisions.reason: The same word that names David's men (verse 5) here names a servant of Nabal's household, probably one of the shepherds who had been with David's men (verses 15-16).

decisions.choice: flew at them with insults
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of a sudden attack while saying it was done with words (m2).

decisions.choice: One of Nabal's servants; yelled insults at them
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear whose servant he was (m3) and gives the sense of the verb (m2).

records.source: וְהָ֣אֲנָשִׁ֔ים טֹבִ֥ים לָ֖נוּ מְאֹ֑ד וְלֹ֤א הָכְלַ֨מְנוּ֙ וְלֹֽא־פָקַ֣דְנוּ מְא֔וּמָה כָּל־יְמֵי֙ הִתְהַלַּ֣כְנוּ אִתָּ֔ם בִּֽהְיוֹתֵ֖נוּ בַּשָּׂדֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And the men [were] good to us very, and not were we humiliated, and not did we miss anything all [the] days we went about with them when we were in the field.
pieces: Yet the men were very good to us. We were not mistreated, and nothing of ours went missing the whole time we were out in the fields with them.

L.15: And the men [were] very good to us, and we were not humiliated, and we did not miss anything all the days we went about with them, when we were in the field.

R.15: But those men were very good to us. They never hurt us, and nothing was stolen from us the whole time we were with them out in the fields.

decisions.choice: we were not humiliated, we did not miss anything: David's own words confirmed
decisions.reason: The servant uses the same words David used in his message (verse 7). What David claimed, Nabal's own people say is true.

decisions.choice: the field: open pasture country
decisions.reason: "Field" means the open country outside the towns, where the flocks grazed.

decisions.choice: mistreated (Balanced); hurt (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

records.source: חוֹמָה֙ הָי֣וּ עָלֵ֔ינוּ גַּם־לַ֖יְלָה גַּם־יוֹמָ֑ם כָּל־יְמֵ֛י הֱיוֹתֵ֥נוּ עִמָּ֖ם רֹעִ֥ים הַצֹּֽאן׃
records.gloss: A wall they were to us both night and also day, all [the] days of our being with them keeping the sheep.
pieces: They were a wall of protection around us night and day, the whole time we were with them looking after the sheep.

L.16: They were a wall to us both by night and by day, all the days we were with them, tending the flock.

R.16: Night and day they protected us like a wall, the whole time we were near them taking care of the sheep.

decisions.choice: a wall: a protection
decisions.reason: A wall kept a town safe from raiders. David's men stood between the shepherds and anyone who would attack them or steal the animals.

decisions.choice: a wall of protection; protected us like a wall
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture means (m1).

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה דְּעִ֤י וּרְאִי֙ מַֽה־תַּעֲשִׂ֔י כִּֽי־כָלְתָ֧ה הָרָעָ֛ה אֶל־אֲדֹנֵ֖ינוּ וְעַ֣ל כָּל־בֵּית֑וֹ וְהוּא֙ בֶּן־בְּלִיַּ֔עַל מִדַּבֵּ֖ר אֵלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And now know and see what you will do, for has been determined the evil against our master and against all his house; and he [is] a son of worthlessness from speaking to him.
pieces: Now think it over and decide what you should do, because disaster has been decided against our master and against his whole household. He is such a worthless man that no one can speak to him."

L.17: And now know and consider what you will do, for evil has been determined against our master and against all his house; and he [is too much] a son of worthlessness [for anyone] to speak to him."

R.17: Now think about what you should do. Something terrible is going to happen to our master and to his whole family. He is so wicked that no one can talk to him!"

decisions.choice: evil has been determined: harm is certain to come
decisions.reason: The verb means to be finished or settled. The servant is sure that David will take revenge, and on the whole household, not on Nabal alone (verse 22).

decisions.choice: a son of worthlessness: a worthless, wicked man
decisions.reason: "Son of" describes a man's character. The phrase is used of Eli's sons (2:12) and of the men who despised Saul (10:27). Abigail calls Nabal the same in verse 25.

decisions.choice: from speaking to him: no one can reason with him
decisions.reason: The Hebrew compares: he is too worthless for anyone to speak to. The servant does not dare to tell Nabal himself, so he goes to Abigail.

decisions.choice: [too much] ... [for anyone]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the words the short Hebrew comparison implies (m3).

records.source: וַתְּמַהֵ֣ר אֲבִיגַ֡יִל וַתִּקַּח֩ מָאתַ֨יִם לֶ֜חֶם וּשְׁנַ֣יִם נִבְלֵי־יַ֗יִן וְחָמֵ֨שׁ צֹ֤אן עֲשׂוּיֹת֙וְחָמֵ֤שׁ סְאִים֙ קָלִ֔י וּמֵאָ֥ה צִמֻּקִ֖ים וּמָאתַ֣יִם דְּבֵלִ֑ים וַתָּ֖שֶׂם עַל־הַחֲמֹרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And hurried Abigail and took two hundred bread and two skins of wine and five sheep prepared and five seahs of roasted grain and a hundred raisin-clusters and two hundred fig-cakes, and put [them] on the donkeys.
pieces: Abigail acted quickly. She took 200 loaves of bread, two skins of wine, five sheep ready to cook, {{units:about a bushel|five seahs}} of roasted grain, 100 clusters of raisins and 200 cakes of pressed figs, and loaded them on donkeys.

L.18: And Abigail hurried and took 200 [loaves of] bread and two skins of wine and five sheep prepared and five seahs of roasted grain and 100 clusters of raisins and 200 cakes of figs, and put [them] on the donkeys.

R.18: Abigail quickly gathered food: 200 loaves of bread, two big skin bags full of wine, five sheep ready for cooking, {{units:about a bushel|five seahs}} of roasted grain, 100 bunches of raisins, and 200 cakes of dried figs. She loaded it all on donkeys.

decisions.choice: Abigail; prepared: the forms read aloud
decisions.reason: In these two words the written consonants (ketiv) and the forms marked to be read aloud (qere) are spelled slightly differently. The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: prepared: slaughtered and dressed, ready to cook
decisions.reason: The sheep were not live animals but already butchered, so that the men could eat at once.

decisions.choice: seah: a dry measure
decisions.reason: A seah was about a third of an ephah, roughly 7 quarts, so five seahs were about a bushel.

decisions.choice: clusters of raisins, cakes of figs: food that keeps
decisions.reason: Dried fruit was pressed into clusters or cakes that kept well and were easy to carry; they were food for travelers and soldiers (30:12; 2 Samuel 16:1).

decisions.choice: {{units:about a bushel|five seahs}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern measure, with the original unit as the setting alternative; Literal keeps "seahs".

decisions.choice: big skin bags full of wine; ready for cooking
decisions.reason: Readable explains the wineskins and the prepared sheep.

records.source: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לִנְעָרֶ֨יהָ֙ עִבְר֣וּ לְפָנַ֔י הִנְנִ֖י אַחֲרֵיכֶ֣ם בָּאָ֑ה וּלְאִישָׁ֥הּ נָבָ֖ל לֹ֥א הִגִּֽידָה׃
records.gloss: And she said to her young men, Pass on before me; look, I [am] coming after you. And to her husband Nabal not she told.
pieces: She said to her servants, "Go on ahead of me; I will follow you." But she said nothing to her husband Nabal.

L.19: And she said to her young men, "Go on before me; look, I [am] coming after you." But she did not tell her husband Nabal.

R.19: She told her servants, "Go on ahead. I will come after you." But she did not tell her husband Nabal about it.

decisions.choice: go on before me: the gift goes ahead to soften the one offended
decisions.reason: Jacob sent his gifts ahead of him in the same way to calm his brother Esau (Genesis 32:17-21).

decisions.choice: she did not tell her husband: she acts without him
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "to her husband Nabal" first for emphasis. Abigail knows that he cannot be reasoned with (verse 17), so she acts on her own.

decisions.choice: her servants
decisions.reason: Her "young men" are the servants of her household.

records.source: וְהָיָ֞ה הִ֣יא׀רֹכֶ֣בֶת עַֽל־הַחֲמ֗וֹר וְיֹרֶ֨דֶת֙ בְּסֵ֣תֶר הָהָ֔ר וְהִנֵּ֤ה דָוִד֙ וַאֲנָשָׁ֔יו יֹרְדִ֖ים לִקְרָאתָ֑הּ וַתִּפְגֹּ֖שׁ אֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And it was, she riding on the donkey and going down in [the] covert of the mountain, and look, David and his men going down to meet her, and she met them.
pieces: As she rode her donkey down into a hidden part of the hill, there were David and his men, coming down in her direction, and she came upon them.

L.20: And it happened, as she was riding on the donkey and going down under cover of the hill, that look, David and his men [were] coming down toward her; and she met them.

R.20: She rode her donkey down the hill, where the slope hid her from view. Suddenly she saw David and his men heading down toward her, and she met them.

decisions.choice: under cover of the hill: in a hidden fold of the hillside
decisions.reason: The word means a hiding place or cover. She came down a ravine or slope where the two parties could not see each other until they met.

decisions.choice: look: a sudden sight
decisions.reason: The word turns the story to what she suddenly saw: David and his men, armed and on their way down, coming straight at her.

decisions.choice: Suddenly she saw
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "look" (m2).

records.source: וְדָוִ֣ד אָמַ֗ר אַךְ֩ לַשֶּׁ֨קֶר שָׁמַ֜רְתִּי אֶֽת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֤ר לָזֶה֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְלֹא־נִפְקַ֥ד מִכָּל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֖וֹ מְא֑וּמָה וַיָּֽשֶׁב־לִ֥י רָעָ֖ה תַּ֥חַת טוֹבָֽה׃
records.gloss: And David had said, Surely in vain I guarded all that [belonged] to this [one] in the wilderness, and not was missing of all that [was] to him anything, and he returned to me evil for good.
pieces: David had just been saying, "It was all for nothing that I protected everything this man had in the wilderness, so that nothing of his went missing. He has paid me back evil for good.

L.21: Now David had said, "Surely in vain I guarded all that this [fellow] has in the wilderness, so that nothing was missing of all that was his; and he has returned me evil for good.

R.21: David had been saying, "What a waste of time it was to guard everything this man owns out in the wilderness! We made sure nothing of his was lost. But he has paid me back with evil for the good I did.

decisions.choice: had said: what David was saying as he marched
decisions.reason: The verb form takes the story back to David's words on the way, before he meets Abigail (verse 13).

decisions.choice: this one: a contemptuous way to speak of Nabal
decisions.reason: David does not name Nabal but says "this one", as Nabal had scorned him (verse 10).

decisions.choice: he has returned me evil for good
decisions.reason: Saul had said the opposite of David: "You have repaid me good, and I have repaid you evil" (24:18). David spared Saul; now he is ready to destroy Nabal.

decisions.choice: for the good I did
decisions.reason: Readable makes the contrast plain.

records.source: כֹּה־יַעֲשֶׂ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים לְאֹיְבֵ֥י דָוִ֖ד וְכֹ֣ה יֹסִ֑יף אִם־אַשְׁאִ֧יר מִכָּל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֛וֹ עַד־הַבֹּ֖קֶר מַשְׁתִּ֥ין בְּקִֽיר׃
records.gloss: Thus may do God to [the] enemies of David, and thus may he add, if I leave of all that [is] to him until the morning one urinating against a wall.
pieces: May God deal with David's enemies ever so severely if by morning I leave alive a single male of all who belong to him!"

L.22: Thus may God do to the enemies of David, and thus may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} add, if I leave of all who belong to him until the morning [even] one who urinates against a wall."

R.22: May God punish David's enemies terribly if I leave even one man or boy of his household alive by morning!"

decisions.choice: thus may God do, and thus may he add: a solemn oath
decisions.reason: This is the form of a curse called down if a promise is not kept (3:17; 14:44; 20:13). The punishment is left unnamed.

decisions.choice: to the enemies of David, as the Hebrew text reads
decisions.reason: In an oath like this the speaker curses himself, so David would be expected to say "to David" (compare 20:16, where a similar softening is found). The ancient Greek translation reads simply "to David". The words "the enemies of" were probably added by scribes so that the curse would not fall on David when he did not carry out his oath. The Hebrew reading is followed, but the sense is a curse on David himself.

decisions.choice: one who urinates against a wall: a male
decisions.reason: This coarse phrase means a male, from the boy upward. It is used in threats to wipe out every male of a household (verse 34; 1 Kings 14:10; 16:11; 21:21; 2 Kings 9:8). David means to kill all the men of Nabal's household.

decisions.choice: all who belong to him: his household and workers
decisions.reason: The threat covers Nabal's family and the men who work for him, not Nabal alone.

decisions.choice: a single male (Balanced); one man or boy (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the plain sense of the coarse idiom (m3); Literal keeps its picture. No gender setting is used, because only males are meant.

decisions.choice: deal with ... ever so severely; punish ... terribly
decisions.reason: The oath is worded as in 3:17, 14:44 and 20:13.

records.source: וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֲבִיגַ֨יִל֙ אֶת־דָּוִ֔ד וַתְּמַהֵ֕ר וַתֵּ֖רֶד מֵעַ֣ל הַחֲמ֑וֹר וַתִּפֹּ֞ל לְאַפֵּ֤י דָוִד֙ עַל־פָּנֶ֔יהָ וַתִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ אָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And saw Abigail David, and she hurried and came down from on the donkey, and fell before [the] face of David on her face and bowed down [to the] ground.
pieces: When Abigail saw David, she quickly got down from her donkey, fell on her face before David and bowed to the ground.

L.23: And Abigail saw David, and she hurried and got down from the donkey, and fell on her face before David, and bowed down to the ground.

R.23: When Abigail saw David, she quickly got off her donkey. She threw herself down in front of him and bowed with her face to the ground.

decisions.choice: fell on her face and bowed to the ground: the deepest honor
decisions.reason: To lie face down on the ground was the honor shown to a king or a great lord (24:9; 2 Samuel 14:4). Abigail treats David as her master and as the king he will be (verse 30).

decisions.choice: before the face of David: in front of David
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "to the nostrils of David", an idiom for in front of him, face to face.

decisions.choice: threw herself down
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain phrase for falling on one's face.

records.source: וַתִּפֹּל֙ עַל־רַגְלָ֔יו וַתֹּ֕אמֶר בִּי־אֲנִ֥י אֲדֹנִ֖י הֶֽעָוֺ֑ן וּֽתְדַבֶּר־נָ֤א אֲמָֽתְךָ֙ בְּאָזְנֶ֔יךָ וּשְׁמַ֕ע אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֥י אֲמָתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And she fell at his feet and said, On me, I, my lord, [is] the guilt; and let speak please your maidservant in your ears, and hear the words of your maidservant.
pieces: She fell at his feet and said, "Let the blame be on me alone, my lord! Please let your servant speak to you, and listen to what your servant has to say.

L.24: And she fell at his feet and said, "On me, me, my lord, [be] the guilt! And please let your maidservant speak in your ears, and hear the words of your maidservant.

R.24: She bowed at his feet and said, "My lord, put all the blame on me! Please let me speak to you. Listen to what I have to say.

decisions.choice: on me be the guilt: I take the blame
decisions.reason: Abigail takes the guilt of the household on herself, offering to bear what Nabal deserves, so that David will listen to her. The woman of Tekoa says the same to David in 2 Samuel 14:9.

decisions.choice: your maidservant: a humble way to speak of oneself
decisions.reason: A woman speaking to a superior called herself his maidservant, as Hannah did to Eli (1:16) and to God (1:11). Abigail uses it again and again in her speech.

decisions.choice: speak in your ears: speak to you directly
decisions.reason: To speak "in someone's ears" is to speak so that he hears, often with the sense of a private word.

decisions.choice: your servant (Balanced); me (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "maidservant". Balanced uses "your servant", as in 1:16. Readable puts Abigail's words in the first person.

records.source: אַל־נָ֣א יָשִׂ֣ים אֲדֹנִ֣י׀אֶת־לִבּ֡וֹ אֶל־אִישׁ֩ הַבְּלִיַּ֨עַל הַזֶּ֜ה עַל־נָבָ֗ל כִּ֤י כִשְׁמוֹ֙ כֶּן־ה֔וּא נָבָ֣ל שְׁמ֔וֹ וּנְבָלָ֖ה עִמּ֑וֹ וַֽאֲנִי֙ אֲמָ֣תְךָ֔ לֹ֥א רָאִ֛יתִי אֶת־נַעֲרֵ֥י אֲדֹנִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁלָֽחְתָּ׃
records.gloss: Not please let set my lord his heart to this man of worthlessness, to Nabal, for as his name, so he [is]: Nabal [is] his name, and folly [is] with him. And I, your maidservant, not did see the young men of my lord whom you sent.
pieces: Please, my lord, pay no attention to this worthless man, Nabal. He is just what his name says. His name is Nabal, Fool, and folly goes with him. But I, your servant, did not see the young men my lord sent.

L.25: Please let my lord not set his heart on this worthless man, on Nabal; for as his name [is], so [is] he: Nabal [is] his name, and folly [is] with him. And I, your maidservant, did not see the young men of my lord whom you sent.

R.25: Please do not pay any attention to Nabal. He is a worthless man. His name means 'Fool', and he is a fool! I did not see the young men you sent, my lord.

decisions.choice: Nabal ... folly: his name and his character match
decisions.reason: Abigail plays on her husband's name: *naval* means a fool (verse 3), and *nevalah*, from the same root, is folly. It is not mere silliness but disgraceful conduct that breaks the bonds of decent life (Genesis 34:7; Judges 19:23; 2 Samuel 13:12).

decisions.choice: as his name is, so is he
decisions.reason: In Israel a name was often taken to say something true about the person who bore it, as Esau says of Jacob (Genesis 27:36).

decisions.choice: set his heart on: take seriously
decisions.reason: To "set the heart" on something is to pay attention to it or be troubled by it (9:20; 2 Samuel 13:33). Abigail asks David not to treat Nabal's insult as worth avenging.

decisions.choice: I did not see: she was not there
decisions.reason: Abigail explains why the messengers got no better answer: she did not see them. Had she known, she implies, she would have received them.

decisions.choice: His name is Nabal, Fool
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the meaning of the name beside it, so that the play on words is not lost.

decisions.choice: His name means 'Fool', and he is a fool!
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name and the play on words in plain words.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֣ה אֲדֹנִ֗י חַי־יְהוָ֤ה וְחֵֽי־נַפְשְׁךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר מְנָעֲךָ֤ יְהוָה֙ מִבּ֣וֹא בְדָמִ֔ים וְהוֹשֵׁ֥עַ יָדְךָ֖ לָ֑ךְ וְעַתָּ֗ה יִֽהְי֤וּ כְנָבָל֙ אֹיְבֶ֔יךָ וְהַֽמְבַקְשִׁ֥ים אֶל־אֲדֹנִ֖י רָעָֽה׃
records.gloss: And now, my lord, [by the] life of Yahweh and [by the] life of your soul, that has restrained you Yahweh from coming into bloodshed and saving your hand for you, and now let be like Nabal your enemies and those seeking against my lord evil.
pieces: Now, my lord, as surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and as surely as you live, it is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who has kept you from shedding blood and from taking revenge with your own hand. So now, may your enemies and all who want to harm my lord be like Nabal.

L.26: And now, my lord, [as] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and [as] your soul lives, since {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has held you back from coming into bloodguilt and from your own hand saving you, now let your enemies and those who seek evil against my lord be like Nabal.

R.26: My lord, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has kept you from killing people and from taking revenge by yourself. I promise this as surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and as surely as you live. Now may your enemies, and everyone who wants to hurt you, end up like Nabal.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh lives and as your soul lives: an oath
decisions.reason: Abigail swears by the life of Yahweh and of David that what she says is true. Jonathan used the same double oath (20:3).

decisions.choice: coming into blood: incurring the guilt of bloodshed
decisions.reason: To "come into blood" is to become guilty of killing. Killing the innocent brought guilt on the killer (Deuteronomy 19:10; verse 31).

decisions.choice: your own hand saving you: taking revenge yourself
decisions.reason: To let one's own hand "save" oneself is to get justice by force instead of leaving it to Yahweh (verses 31, 33; Judges 7:2). David had refused to do this to Saul (24:13).

decisions.choice: Yahweh has held you back: Abigail's coming is God's doing
decisions.reason: Abigail speaks as if it has already happened: by sending her, Yahweh has stopped David. David agrees (verses 32-34).

decisions.choice: may your enemies be like Nabal
decisions.reason: The wish hints at what will happen to Nabal: Yahweh strikes him down (verse 38).

decisions.choice: I promise this as surely as the LORD lives
decisions.reason: Readable states what Yahweh has done first and then gives the oath as a promise that it is true (m1).

records.source: וְעַתָּה֙ הַבְּרָכָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את אֲשֶׁר־הֵבִ֥יא שִׁפְחָתְךָ֖ לַֽאדֹנִ֑י וְנִתְּנָה֙ לַנְּעָרִ֔ים הַמִּֽתְהַלְּכִ֖ים בְּרַגְלֵ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי׃
records.gloss: And now this blessing which has brought your maidservant to my lord, let it be given to the young men who go about at [the] feet of my lord.
pieces: Now let the young men who follow my lord be given this gift that your servant has brought to him.

L.27: And now this blessing that your maidservant has brought to my lord, let it be given to the young men who walk at the feet of my lord.

R.27: I have brought a gift for you, my lord. Please let it be given to the young men who follow you.

decisions.choice: this blessing: this gift
decisions.reason: A "blessing" can be a gift given with good will (30:26; Genesis 33:11).

decisions.choice: walk at the feet of my lord: follow him
decisions.reason: Those who go "at someone's feet" are his followers or attendants (verse 42; Judges 4:10).

decisions.choice: given to the young men: a gift for David's band
decisions.reason: Abigail modestly offers the food to David's men, the ones Nabal refused (verses 8, 11), rather than to David himself.

decisions.choice: a gift
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain word (m1).

records.source: שָׂ֥א נָ֖א לְפֶ֣שַׁע אֲמָתֶ֑ךָ כִּ֣י עָשֹֽׂה־יַעֲשֶׂה֩ יְהוָ֨ה לַֽאדֹנִ֜י בַּ֣יִת נֶאֱמָ֗ן כִּי־מִלְחֲמ֤וֹת יְהוָה֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י נִלְחָ֔ם וְרָעָ֛ה לֹא־תִמָּצֵ֥א בְךָ֖ מִיָּמֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Forgive please the transgression of your maidservant, for surely will make Yahweh for my lord a house enduring, for [the] battles of Yahweh my lord [is] fighting, and evil not will be found in you from your days.
pieces: Please forgive your servant's offense. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will certainly make my lord a house that lasts, because my lord fights the battles of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and no wrong will be found in you as long as you live.

L.28: Please forgive the transgression of your maidservant, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will certainly make for my lord an enduring house, because my lord is fighting the battles of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and evil will not be found in you all your days.

R.28: Please forgive me for what I have done wrong. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will surely give you a family of kings that will last, because you fight {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s battles. And no one will find any wrong in you as long as you live.

decisions.choice: the transgression of your maidservant: Abigail asks pardon for herself
decisions.reason: She has taken Nabal's guilt on herself (verse 24), and now asks David to forgive it, as well as her boldness in speaking.

decisions.choice: an enduring house: a lasting royal line
decisions.reason: "House" here means a family line. God promised "an enduring house" to a faithful priest (2:35) and later promised David that his house would endure forever (2 Samuel 7:16; 1 Kings 11:38).

decisions.choice: the battles of Yahweh: Israel's wars fought for God
decisions.reason: Saul had sent David to "fight the battles of Yahweh" (18:17). David's wars against Israel's enemies are Yahweh's wars.

decisions.choice: evil will not be found in you: no wrongdoing
alternatives: no disaster will come upon you
decisions.reason: The word can mean wrongdoing or disaster. Here it most likely means that David will do no wrong, which fits Abigail's plea that he not take revenge (verses 26, 31). It could also mean that no harm will come to him.

decisions.choice: a family of kings that will last
decisions.reason: Readable says what the "house" means (m2).

records.source: וַיָּ֤קָם אָדָם֙ לִרְדָפְךָ֔ וּלְבַקֵּ֖שׁ אֶת־נַפְשֶׁ֑ךָ וְֽהָיְתָה֩ נֶ֨פֶשׁ אֲדֹנִ֜י צְרוּרָ֣ה׀בִּצְר֣וֹר הַחַיִּ֗ים אֵ֚ת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ וְאֵ֨ת נֶ֤פֶשׁ אֹיְבֶ֨יךָ֙ יְקַלְּעֶ֔נָּה בְּת֖וֹךְ כַּ֥ף הַקָּֽלַע׃
records.gloss: And has risen a man to pursue you and to seek your life, and will be the life of my lord bound in the bundle of the living with Yahweh your God; and the life of your enemies he will sling out in [the] middle of [the] hollow of the sling.
pieces: If anyone rises up to pursue you and to take your life, the life of my lord will be bound safe in the bundle of the living in the care of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. But the lives of your enemies {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will hurl away as from the pocket of a sling.

L.29: And [if] a man rises to pursue you and to seek your life, then the life of my lord will be bound in the bundle of the living with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God; but the life of your enemies {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will sling out from the hollow of the sling.

R.29: Someone may come after you to kill you. But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will keep your life safe with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, like a treasure tied up in a bag. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will throw away the lives of your enemies like stones from a sling.

decisions.choice: bound in the bundle of the living: kept safe by Yahweh
alternatives: listed in the record of the living
decisions.reason: A bundle was a pouch in which something precious was tied up and kept, such as money (Genesis 42:35; Proverbs 7:20). David's life will be held safe, like a treasure, in Yahweh's keeping. Some take the bundle as a list or record of those who are to live, like the book of Exodus 32:32. The phrase speaks of David being kept alive; later Jewish readers used it of life with God after death.

decisions.choice: if a man rises: a condition
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets out a case: should anyone rise up against David, then what follows is sure. The pursuer is not named, but Saul is in view (23:15; 24:15).

decisions.choice: sling out from the hollow of the sling
decisions.reason: As David slung a stone at Goliath (17:40, 49), Yahweh will fling David's enemies away. The sling's pocket held the stone before it was let fly.

decisions.choice: with Yahweh: in Yahweh's keeping
decisions.reason: "With" means near him and under his care.

decisions.choice: bound safe; in the care of
decisions.reason: Balanced adds what the picture implies (m1, m4).

decisions.choice: like a treasure tied up in a bag
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the bundle (m1) instead of reproducing it.

records.source: וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי־יַעֲשֶׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לַֽאדֹנִ֔י כְּכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר אֶת־הַטּוֹבָ֖ה עָלֶ֑יךָ וְצִוְּךָ֥ לְנָגִ֖יד עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And it will be when will do Yahweh for my lord according to all that he has spoken, the good concerning you, and has appointed you as ruler over Israel,
pieces: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done for my lord every good thing {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has promised you, and has made you ruler over Israel,

L.30: And it will be, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does for my lord according to all the good that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has spoken concerning you, and appoints you ruler over Israel,

R.30: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will do for you all the good things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has promised, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make you the leader of Israel.

decisions.choice: ruler: the one Yahweh appoints to lead
decisions.reason: The word names the leader whom Yahweh chooses for his people (9:16; 10:1; 13:14). Saul's own words show that David will hold this place (24:21).

decisions.choice: all the good he has spoken concerning you
decisions.reason: Abigail speaks of a promise already known: Samuel had anointed David (16:13), and Jonathan and Saul had both said he would be king (23:17; 24:21).

decisions.choice: the sentence goes on into verse 31
decisions.reason: Verse 30 states the time ("when Yahweh has done ..."), and verse 31 what follows. It is one sentence across two verses.

decisions.choice: ends with a comma
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the sentence running into verse 31.

decisions.choice: two sentences
decisions.reason: Readable makes verse 30 a statement of its own and starts verse 31 with "When that happens".

records.gloss: and not will be this to you for staggering and for stumbling of heart for my lord, and to pour out blood without cause and for my lord saving himself. And will do good Yahweh to my lord, and you will remember your maidservant.
pieces: my lord will not have this on his mind, no troubled conscience for having shed blood without cause or for having taken revenge himself. And when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has dealt well with my lord, remember your servant."

L.31: this will not be to you a staggering or a stumbling of heart for my lord, either to have poured out blood without cause or for my lord to have saved himself. And when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does good to my lord, then remember your maidservant."

R.31: When that happens, you will not feel sorry or guilty for having killed people for no reason, or for having taken revenge yourself. And when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has been good to you, please remember me."

decisions.choice: a staggering or a stumbling of heart: regret and a troubled conscience
decisions.reason: Both words picture tripping or reeling. A "stumbling of heart" is the inner trouble that comes from guilt, like David's later "heart striking him" (24:6; 2 Samuel 24:10).

decisions.choice: pouring out blood without cause: killing the innocent
decisions.reason: "Without cause" means without just reason. To kill Nabal's household would make David guilty of innocent blood (19:5).

decisions.choice: remember your maidservant
decisions.reason: Abigail asks David to show her favor once he is king, as Joseph asked Pharaoh's cupbearer (Genesis 40:14). In the end David marries her (verse 42).

decisions.choice: feel sorry or guilty
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the pictures (m1).

decisions.choice: your servant (Balanced); me (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 24.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר דָּוִ֖ד לַאֲבִיגַ֑ל בָּר֤וּךְ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֧ר שְׁלָחֵ֛ךְ הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה לִקְרָאתִֽי׃
records.gloss: And said David to Abigail, Blessed [be] Yahweh, the God of Israel, who sent you this day to meet me.
pieces: David answered Abigail, "Blessed be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, who has sent you out to meet me today.

L.32: And David said to Abigail, "Blessed [be] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, who sent you this day to meet me.

R.32: David said to Abigail, "Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel! He sent you to meet me today.

decisions.choice: blessed be Yahweh: praise and thanks to God
decisions.reason: To "bless" God is to praise and thank him for what he has done.

decisions.choice: who sent you: David sees God's hand in her coming
decisions.reason: David agrees with Abigail (verse 26): it was Yahweh who sent her to stop him.

decisions.choice: Praise
decisions.reason: Readable uses "praise", the plain sense of blessing God (m1).

records.heading: Abigail becomes David's wife

records.source: וּבָר֥וּךְ טַעְמֵ֖ךְ וּבְרוּכָ֣ה אָ֑תְּ אֲשֶׁ֨ר כְּלִתִ֜נִי הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ מִבּ֣וֹא בְדָמִ֔ים וְהֹשֵׁ֥עַ יָדִ֖י לִֽי׃
records.gloss: And blessed [be] your discernment, and blessed [be] you, who have restrained me this day from coming into bloodshed and saving my hand for me.
pieces: Blessed be your good judgment, and blessed be you, for keeping me today from shedding blood and from taking revenge with my own hand.

L.33: And blessed [be] your discernment, and blessed [be] you, who have kept me this day from coming into bloodguilt and from my own hand saving me.

R.33: Your good sense is a blessing, and may you be blessed! Today you have kept me from killing people and from taking revenge myself.

decisions.choice: your discernment: your good judgment
decisions.reason: The word means taste, and so discernment or good sense (Psalm 119:66). David praises the wisdom the narrator noted at the start (verse 3).

decisions.choice: kept me from coming into bloodguilt: Abigail's own words
decisions.reason: David repeats what Abigail said Yahweh had done (verse 26), now saying it of her: God has worked through her.

decisions.choice: Your good sense is a blessing, and may you be blessed!
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the two blessings in plain words.

records.source: וְאוּלָ֗ם חַי־יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר מְנָעַ֔נִי מֵהָרַ֖ע אֹתָ֑ךְ כִּ֣י׀לוּלֵ֣י מִהַ֗רְתְּ וַתָּבֹאת֙ לִקְרָאתִ֔י כִּ֣י אִם־נוֹתַ֧ר לְנָבָ֛ל עַד־א֥וֹר הַבֹּ֖קֶר מַשְׁתִּ֥ין בְּקִֽיר׃
records.gloss: And however, [by the] life of Yahweh, the God of Israel, who has held me back from harming you, for if not you had hurried and come to meet me, surely not would have been left to Nabal until [the] light of the morning one urinating against a wall.
pieces: But as surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, lives, who held me back from doing you harm, if you had not hurried out to meet me, not a single male belonging to Nabal would have been left alive by daybreak."

L.34: But truly, [as] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, lives, who has held me back from harming you, if you had not hurried and come to meet me, surely there would not have been left to Nabal by the light of morning [even] one who urinates against a wall."

R.34: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, has kept me from hurting you. As surely as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives, if you had not hurried to meet me, not one man or boy in Nabal's household would have been alive by morning."

decisions.choice: harming you: Abigail too was in danger
decisions.reason: David would have harmed Abigail as well, since she belonged to Nabal's household. Yahweh's restraint saved her too.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh lives: an oath
decisions.reason: David swears to the truth of what he says, as Abigail did (verse 26).

decisions.choice: and you had come: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) have an unusual spelling of this verb; the form marked to be read aloud (qere) is the ordinary "and you came". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: one who urinates against a wall: a male
decisions.reason: As in verse 22.

decisions.choice: a single male (Balanced); one man or boy (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 22.

decisions.choice: the LORD ... has kept me; As surely as he lives
decisions.reason: Readable states what Yahweh has done first and then gives the oath.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֤ח דָּוִד֙ מִיָּדָ֔הּ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־הֵבִ֖יאָה ל֑וֹ וְלָ֣הּ אָמַ֗ר עֲלִ֤י לְשָׁלוֹם֙ לְבֵיתֵ֔ךְ רְאִי֙ שָׁמַ֣עְתִּי בְקוֹלֵ֔ךְ וָאֶשָּׂ֖א פָּנָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: And took David from her hand what she had brought to him, and to her he said, Go up in peace to your house; see, I have listened to your voice and have lifted your face.
pieces: Then David accepted what she had brought him from her hand, and told her, "Go back home in peace. I have listened to what you said, and I grant your request."

L.35: And David took from her hand what she had brought him, and to her he said, "Go up in peace to your house. See, I have listened to your voice and lifted up your face."

R.35: Then David accepted the gifts she had brought him. He told her, "Go home and do not worry. I have listened to you, and I will do what you asked."

decisions.choice: lifted up your face: granted your request
decisions.reason: To "lift someone's face" is to receive a person with favor and grant what is asked (Genesis 19:21; 32:21).

decisions.choice: took from her hand: accepted the gift
decisions.reason: Accepting a gift was a sign of peace between two parties (Genesis 33:10-11). David's anger is over.

decisions.choice: go up in peace: go home safe
decisions.reason: A farewell that also promises that no harm will come to her or her household.

decisions.choice: Go home and do not worry; I will do what you asked
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the farewell and of the idiom (m1, m3).

records.source: וַתָּבֹ֣א אֲבִיגַ֣יִל׀אֶל־נָבָ֡ל וְהִנֵּה־לוֹ֩ מִשְׁתֶּ֨ה בְּבֵית֜וֹ כְּמִשְׁתֵּ֣ה הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וְלֵ֤ב נָבָל֙ ט֣וֹב עָלָ֔יו וְה֥וּא שִׁכֹּ֖ר עַד־מְאֹ֑ד וְלֹֽא־הִגִּ֣ידָה לּ֗וֹ דָּבָ֥ר קָטֹ֛ן וְגָד֖וֹל עַד־א֥וֹר הַבֹּֽקֶר׃
records.gloss: And came Abigail to Nabal, and look, to him [was] a feast in his house like [the] feast of the king, and [the] heart of Nabal [was] good upon him, and he [was] drunk to very [much]; and not she told him a thing small or great until [the] light of the morning.
pieces: When Abigail came back to Nabal, he was holding a feast in his house, a feast fit for a king. Nabal was in high spirits and very drunk, so she told him nothing at all until daybreak.

L.36: And Abigail came to Nabal, and look, he [was holding] a feast in his house like the feast of a king, and the heart of Nabal [was] merry within him, and he [was] very drunk. So she did not tell him anything, small or great, until the light of morning.

R.36: When Abigail came home, Nabal was having a big party at his house, like a party for a king. He was happy and very drunk. So she did not tell him anything until the next morning.

decisions.choice: a feast like the feast of a king: Nabal lives like a king
decisions.reason: The shearing feast (verse 2) is lavish. The story contrasts Nabal, who feasts like a king, with David, the future king, to whom he refused bread (verse 11). Absalom's shearing feast in 2 Samuel 13:23-28 is also a scene of drunkenness.

decisions.choice: the heart of Nabal was good: he was merry with wine
decisions.reason: A "good heart" here means high spirits from drinking (Judges 16:25; 2 Samuel 13:28; Esther 1:10).

decisions.choice: small or great: nothing at all
decisions.reason: The pair means nothing of any kind (20:2; 22:15).

decisions.choice: a feast fit for a king
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the comparison.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י בַבֹּ֗קֶר בְּצֵ֤את הַיַּ֨יִן֙ מִנָּבָ֔ל וַתַּגֶּד־ל֣וֹ אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיָּ֤מָת לִבּוֹ֙ בְּקִרְבּ֔וֹ וְה֖וּא הָיָ֥ה לְאָֽבֶן׃
records.gloss: And it was in the morning, when went out the wine from Nabal, and told him his wife these things, and died his heart within him, and he became stone.
pieces: In the morning, when Nabal was sober, his wife told him all this. His heart failed him, and he became like a stone.

L.37: And it happened in the morning, when the wine had gone out of Nabal, that his wife told him these things; and his heart died within him, and he became a stone.

R.37: The next morning, when Nabal was sober again, his wife told him what had happened. His heart failed him, and he lay there like a stone.

decisions.choice: when the wine had gone out of Nabal: when he was sober
decisions.reason: The picture is of the wine leaving him as he slept it off (compare 1:14).

decisions.choice: his heart died within him, and he became a stone: a sudden collapse
decisions.reason: Hearing how close he had come to death, Nabal collapsed and could not move. It may describe a stroke or a failure of the heart, which left him helpless until he died ten days later (verse 38); the text does not say exactly what happened. The heart was also the seat of courage, so the words may also say that his spirit was crushed.

decisions.choice: His heart failed him; like a stone
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a common phrase for the heart's failing and make the comparison plain.

records.source: וַיְהִ֖י כַּעֲשֶׂ֣רֶת הַיָּמִ֑ים וַיִּגֹּ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־נָבָ֖ל וַיָּמֹֽת׃
records.gloss: And it was about ten days, and struck Yahweh Nabal, and he died.
pieces: About ten days later {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck Nabal, and he died.

L.38: And it happened after about ten days that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck Nabal, and he died.

R.38: About ten days later, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck Nabal down, and he died.

decisions.choice: Yahweh struck Nabal: his death is God's judgment
decisions.reason: The narrator says that Yahweh himself struck Nabal. What Abigail asked David to leave to Yahweh (verses 26, 31), Yahweh has done. David says the same about Saul later (26:10).

decisions.choice: about ten days: the time after Nabal's collapse
decisions.reason: The ten days are counted from the morning when Nabal heard the news (verse 37).

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע דָּוִד֮ כִּ֣י מֵ֣ת נָבָל֒ וַיֹּ֡אמֶר בָּר֣וּךְ יְהוָ֡ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר רָב֩ אֶת־רִ֨יב חֶרְפָּתִ֜י מִיַּ֣ד נָבָ֗ל וְאֶת־עַבְדּוֹ֙ חָשַׂ֣ךְ מֵֽרָעָ֔ה וְאֵת֙ רָעַ֣ת נָבָ֔ל הֵשִׁ֥יב יְהוָ֖ה בְּרֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח דָּוִד֙ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר בַּאֲבִיגַ֔יִל לְקַחְתָּ֥הּ ל֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And heard David that had died Nabal, and said, Blessed [be] Yahweh, who has pleaded [the] case of my reproach from [the] hand of Nabal, and his servant he has kept back from evil, and the evil of Nabal has returned Yahweh on his head. And sent David and spoke to Abigail to take her for himself as wife.
pieces: When David heard that Nabal had died, he said, "Blessed be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who has taken up my case against Nabal for the insult he gave me, and has kept {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant from doing evil. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has brought Nabal's evil back on his own head." Then David sent word to Abigail, asking her to become his wife.

L.39: And David heard that Nabal had died, and he said, "Blessed [be] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who has pleaded the case of my insult from the hand of Nabal, and has kept back {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slave from evil; and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has returned the evil of Nabal on his [own] head." And David sent and spoke to Abigail, to take her for himself as a wife.

R.39: When David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, "Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! Nabal insulted me, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has judged him for it. He kept me, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant, from doing wrong, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has punished Nabal for the evil he did." Then David sent messengers to Abigail to ask her to marry him.

decisions.choice: pleaded the case of my insult: took up my cause
decisions.reason: To "plead someone's case" is to act as his advocate and judge, as David had asked Yahweh to do against Saul (24:16). Yahweh has defended David's honor against Nabal's insult.

decisions.choice: returned the evil of Nabal on his own head
decisions.reason: Wrongdoing comes back on the one who did it (Judges 9:57; 1 Kings 2:44). Nabal's punishment fits what he did.

decisions.choice: kept his servant from evil: from taking revenge
decisions.reason: David sees that Yahweh kept him from doing wrong, through Abigail (verses 32-34).

decisions.choice: spoke to Abigail to take her as a wife: a proposal of marriage
decisions.reason: David sent messengers to ask for her hand (verse 40). As a widow, Abigail could give her own answer.

decisions.choice: his slave
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "slave", as with "my servant David" elsewhere; Balanced and Readable have "servant".

decisions.choice: Nabal insulted me, but the LORD has judged him for it
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long blessing into short sentences and states the insult first.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ עַבְדֵ֥י דָוִ֛ד אֶל־אֲבִיגַ֖יִל הַכַּרְמֶ֑לָה וַיְדַבְּר֤וּ אֵלֶ֨יהָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר דָּוִד֙ שְׁלָחָ֣נוּ אֵלַ֔יִךְ לְקַחְתֵּ֥ךְ ל֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And came [the] servants of David to Abigail to Carmel, and spoke to her saying, David has sent us to you to take you to him as wife.
pieces: David's servants came to Abigail at Carmel and said to her, "David has sent us to you to take you to be his wife."

L.40: And the servants of David came to Abigail at Carmel, and they spoke to her, saying, "David has sent us to you to take you to him as a wife."

R.40: David's servants went to Abigail at Carmel. They told her, "David sent us to bring you to him to be his wife."

decisions.choice: at Carmel: Abigail is still at Nabal's estate
decisions.reason: Nabal's flocks and property were at Carmel (verse 2), and Abigail was there.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: David's envoys are "servants" at every level, as in verse 10.

records.source: וַתָּ֕קָם וַתִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ אַפַּ֖יִם אָ֑רְצָה וַתֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֤ה אֲמָֽתְךָ֙ לְשִׁפְחָ֔ה לִרְחֹ֕ץ רַגְלֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי׃
records.gloss: And she arose and bowed down [with] face to [the] ground and said, Look, your maidservant [is] as a slave-girl to wash [the] feet of [the] servants of my lord.
pieces: She got up and bowed down with her face to the ground, and said, "Your servant is ready to be a maid who washes the feet of my lord's servants."

L.41: And she arose and bowed down [with her] face to the ground, and said, "Look, your maidservant [is] a slave girl to wash the feet of the servants of my lord."

R.41: Abigail got up and bowed down with her face to the ground. She said, "I am ready to serve. I would even wash the feet of my lord's servants."

decisions.choice: slave girl: the lowest of servants
decisions.reason: Abigail calls herself first a maidservant and then a slave girl, a still humbler word (1:18). Washing the feet of guests was the work of the lowest servant.

decisions.choice: look, your maidservant is a slave girl: she accepts
decisions.reason: The words are a humble way of saying yes. Abigail accepts David's offer and puts herself at his service, even to his servants.

decisions.choice: a maid (Balanced); serve (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "servant" and "maid"; Literal keeps "slave girl" for the humbler word.

records.source: וַתְּמַהֵ֞ר וַתָּ֣קָם אֲבִיגַ֗יִל וַתִּרְכַּב֙ עַֽל־הַחֲמ֔וֹר וְחָמֵשׁ֙ נַעֲרֹתֶ֔יהָ הַהֹלְכ֖וֹת לְרַגְלָ֑הּ וַתֵּ֗לֶךְ אַֽחֲרֵי֙ מַלְאֲכֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד וַתְּהִי־ל֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And hurried and arose Abigail and rode on the donkey, and five her maids who went at her feet; and she went after [the] messengers of David and became to him as wife.
pieces: Abigail quickly got up and mounted her donkey, with her five maids attending her. She followed David's messengers and became his wife.

L.42: And Abigail hurried and arose and rode on the donkey, with five of her maids who walked at her feet; and she went after the messengers of David and became his wife.

R.42: Abigail quickly got ready and rode off on her donkey, with her five servant girls walking with her. She went with David's messengers and became David's wife.

decisions.choice: who walked at her feet: who attended her
decisions.reason: As in verse 27, those "at someone's feet" are attendants.

decisions.choice: five maids: a woman of standing
decisions.reason: Abigail comes with her own attendants, as a wealthy woman would.

decisions.choice: servant girls
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain word for her maids.

records.source: וְאֶת־אֲחִינֹ֛עַם לָקַ֥ח דָּוִ֖ד מִֽיִּזְרְעֶ֑אל וַתִּהְיֶ֛יןָ גַּֽם־שְׁתֵּיהֶ֥ן ל֖וֹ לְנָשִֽׁים׃ס
records.gloss: And Ahinoam David had taken from Jezreel, and they became also both of them to him as wives.
pieces: David had also married Ahinoam of Jezreel, so both of them became his wives.

L.43: And David had taken Ahinoam from Jezreel, and the two of them also became his wives.

R.43: David had already married Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel. So both women became his wives.

decisions.choice: Jezreel: a town in the hill country of Judah
decisions.reason: This Jezreel is the town near Maon and Carmel (Joshua 15:55-56), not the better-known Jezreel in the north (29:1).

decisions.choice: had taken: before he married Abigail
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts Ahinoam first and uses a form that looks back. Ahinoam is named first in later lists too (27:3; 2 Samuel 3:2). Saul's wife had the same name (14:50), but the text does not connect them.

decisions.choice: married
decisions.reason: "Take" a woman means to marry her.

records.source: וְשָׁא֗וּל נָתַ֛ן אֶת־מִיכַ֥ל בִּתּ֖וֹ אֵ֣שֶׁת דָּוִ֑ד לְפַלְטִ֥י בֶן־לַ֖יִשׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִגַּלִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And Saul had given Michal his daughter, [the] wife of David, to Palti son of Laish, who [was] from Gallim.
pieces: Saul, for his part, had given David's wife Michal, his own daughter, to Palti son of Laish, who was from Gallim.

L.44: And Saul had given Michal his daughter, David's wife, to Palti son of Laish, who [was] from Gallim.

R.44: But Saul had taken his daughter Michal, who was David's wife, and given her to another man, Palti son of Laish, from the town of Gallim.

decisions.choice: Michal, David's wife: married to another man
decisions.reason: Michal had married David (18:27) and helped him escape (19:11-17). While David was a fugitive, Saul gave her to another man. David later took her back (2 Samuel 3:13-16), where her second husband is called Paltiel.

decisions.choice: Gallim: a village of Benjamin
decisions.reason: Gallim lay near Saul's town Gibeah, north of Jerusalem (Isaiah 10:30).

decisions.choice: had given: before this point in the story
decisions.reason: The verb looks back. By giving David's wife to another man, Saul cut David's tie to the royal house.

decisions.choice: had taken ... and given her to another man
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that Michal was taken from David.
